summary: Round-2 MAJOR (unpaired surrogate) is genuinely closed -- verified by exhaustive fuzz over every Unicode code point, every lone UTF-16 unit and surrogate pairs in both orders: 2,364,661 accepted values, zero round trips that are not identity. Round-2 minors F2, F4 and F5 are genuinely closed -- each guard now dies to a named test. Round-2 minor F3 is NOT closed: its new test never reaches the guard it names, and deleting that guard survives all 21 tests. 30 mutations run; 2 survivors, 1 of them a true equivalent mutant.

findings.title: The fix for round-2 minor F3 is an equivalent-mutant test -- the same defect class F2 was raised for, one round later. Deleting stringField's `end < 0` guard still survives all 21 tests.
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED. Mutation: delete the three lines `if (end < 0) { throw new IOException("lease has an unterminated " + name + ": " + s); }` from Lease.java:229-232. Result: `./gradlew :format:test --tests binjava.format.LeaseTest` -> tests=21 failures=0. The mutant SURVIVES.

WHY: the test's input is `{"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"`. Its last character is a quote, not `}`, so decode's shape guard at Lease.java:186 rejects it with "not a lease object" and control NEVER REACHES stringField. Probed against the unmutated code:
  {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"        -> IOException: not a lease object: ...
  {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"pod1}   -> IOException: lease has an unterminated holderPodId: ...
The test passes for the wrong reason, exactly as the three brace-guard tests did in round 2.

THE BUG IT CLAIMS TO PIN IS STILL REACHABLE. With the guard deleted, probed directly:
  {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"pod1}                            -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: Range [26, -1) out of bounds for length 31
  {"epoch":1,"holderPodId":"p","holderEndpoint":"e}          -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: Range [47, -1) out of bounds for length 49
Unchecked, out of a method declared `throws IOException`, which is precisely what M4.3b's `catch (IOException)` on the recovery path would miss -- the failure round 2 named.

SECOND-ORDER: backlog.md's M4.3 row now asserts of this exact case "...escaped as UNCHECKED exceptions from a method declared `throws IOException`, which M4.3b's `catch` would miss ... All fixed". Measurement says the test does not hold that claim up. Under non-negotiable 4 the tree should not carry a claim that a check exists when it was measured not to.

REMEDY, VERIFIED: change the literal at LeaseTest.java:290 from `"{\"epoch\":1,\"holderPodId\":\""` to `"{\"epoch\":1,\"holderPodId\":\"pod1}"` -- braced, so it passes the shape guard and lands on stringField. Applied together with the guard deletion: failures=1, KILLED-BY aLeaseTruncatedInsideAStringValueFailsAsIoNotAnUncheckedException. Applied without the deletion: green. One test literal, no production change, no new prose surface.

findings.title: The emoji round trip does not kill the mutation the code comment names it against. U+1F600 truncates to a Private Use character, not a surrogate.
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED. Mutation: `cp -> cp >= 0xD800 && cp <= 0xDFFF` -> `cp -> Character.isSurrogate((char) cp)` at Lease.java:247 -- literally the mutation Lease.java:244-246 and the backlog row say the range form exists to survive. Result: tests=21 failures=0. The mutant SURVIVES, because `(char) 0x1F600 == 0xF600`, which is Private Use Area and not a surrogate, so the emoji is still accepted.

The assertion is NOT worthless -- it kills the realistic wrong implementation: mutating to `value.chars().anyMatch(c -> c >= 0xD800 && c <= 0xDFFF)` (scan UTF-16 units instead of code points) gives failures=1 KILLED-BY anUnpairedSurrogateIsRefusedThoughAValidAstralPairIsNot, and so do both charset mutations (encode/decode ISO_8859_1). But the specific claim in the comment and the backlog is not backed by measurement.

REMEDY: add one astral code point whose low 16 bits fall in the surrogate range -- U+1D800 is `"\uD837\uDC00"` -- alongside the emoji. `(char) 0x1D800 == 0xD800`, so the cast mutation refuses it and the test dies; the range form accepts it and the test passes. Either fix the test or drop the claim from the comment and the backlog row; a mutation named in prose and never run is the thing this review exists to catch.

verified_closed: Round-2 MAJOR (unpaired surrogate). Removing the guard (`if (false)`) -> failures=1, KILLED-BY anUnpairedSurrogateIsRefusedThoughAValidAstralPairIsNot. Dropping the holderEndpoint call site -> failures=3.

Exhaustive hunt for any accepted value whose round trip is not identity: every code point U+0000..U+10FFFF embedded and solo in both fields; every lone UTF-16 unit 0x0000..0xFFFF; surrogate pairs in both orders; BOM U+FEFF, U+2028, U+2029, NEL U+0085, DEL, noncharacters U+FFFE/U+FFFF/U+1FFFE, combining marks, ZWJ, RTL override, NBSP, ideographic space, U+1D800 (astral whose low bits are in the surrogate range), U+10FFFF; strings of 1, 2, 1000, 100k and 1M chars including 1M emoji; numeric extremes to Long.MAX_VALUE. accepted=2364661 refused=45579 NOT-IDENTITY=0. Empty podId refused; empty endpoint accepted and round-trips.

Round-2 minor F2 (three shape guards were equivalent mutants). Each deleted individually now dies: `s.length() < 2` -> aMalformedOrTruncatedLeaseIsRefused; `s.charAt(0) != '{'` -> aLeaseTruncatedByASingleByteIsRefused; `s.charAt(s.length()-1) != '}'` -> aLeaseTruncatedByASingleByteIsRefused. stringField's missing-field guard -> aLeaseMissingAStringFieldIsRefused.
Round-2 minor F4 (decode(null)). `if (bytes == null)` -> `if (false)` -> failures=1, KILLED-BY decodingNullFailsAsIoNotAnUncheckedException.
Round-2 minor F5 (strip() unpinned). Removing `.strip()` -> failures=1, KILLED-BY surroundingWhitespaceIsToleratedBecauseAHandEditedLeaseCarriesANewline.

Semantics: `>=` -> `>` in isExpiredAt killed; epoch+1 -> epoch+2 in takenOverBy killed; renewedUntil bumping the epoch killed; canonical comparison disabled killed; epoch<0 and expiresAtMillis<0 boundary shifted to -1 both killed; isBlank guard killed; quote, backslash and control-char checks each killed individually; rejectUnrepresentable loop bound shortened by one killed; stringField closing-quote off-by-one killed; decode string-argument swap killed; encode field-name typo killed by six tests.

Tier and hygiene: T0 throughout, correct per testing.md rule 1. No Thread.sleep, no fixed port, no system temp, no mock. No pre-existing assertion weakened -- both Java files are new. Suite 453 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. check-tdd green: 21 new tests, all observed failing first, unchanged since. Tree restored after every mutation; `git diff` empty and staged sha256 unchanged at b4dbd3a0.
equivalent_mutants_not_findings: Deleting longField's `end == from` guard survives (tests=21 failures=0), but it is behaviourally equivalent: `Long.parseLong("")` throws NumberFormatException, which the catch below converts to the same IOException. Only the message differs. No test should be added for it.
`.strip()` -> `.trim()` survives, equivalent for the ASCII whitespace the cat/echo story is about; they differ only on Unicode whitespace such as U+3000.
